Goblincore theme

Source: R/theme_goblincore.R
theme_goblincore.Rd

Goblincore celebrates the less pretty side of nature: moss, mushrooms, snails, and found objects. Goblincore is a grungier, moodier cousin of cottagecore. It grew on TikTok in 2021 and ties into Gen Z's interest in nature and sustainability. The trend pulls people away from screens and into forests and empty lots. Coverage reads its anti consumerist attitude and love of imperfection as a response to an unsettling, post pandemic world.

Usage

theme_goblincore(
  base_size = 15,
  base_family = register_font("Arial", "Arial.ttf", "Arial Bold.ttf"),
  title_family = register_font("Luminari", "Luminari.ttf"),
  mode = c("dark", "light")
)

Arguments

base_size

Base font size. Defaults to 15.

base_family

Base font family. Defaults to Arial when it's available on the system, otherwise "sans".

title_family

Title font family. Defaults to Luminari when it's available, otherwise "sans".

mode

"dark" (the default) or "light".

Value

A ggplot2 theme object.

Details

The palette follows mud, moss, and fungi in natural earth tones: moss green, toadstool red, mushroom beige, lichen sage, mud brown, and olive on soil black.

Use mode = "light" for a light background with dark text and darker marks.

See also

Goblincore on Wikipedia.

Examples

library(ggplot2)
ggplot(data.frame(x = c("a", "b", "b")), aes(x = x, fill = x)) +
  geom_bar() +
  labs(title = "Goblincore") +
  theme_goblincore(base_family = "sans", title_family = "sans")
